verdict.rationale: Cursor documents real execution isolation: Cloud Agents run in isolated VMs with full dev environments where they build and test changes, and Auto-review run mode sandboxes shell commands under file and network limits. This is sandbox isolation, not just a dry run (print mode without --force only proposes changes). However, nothing documents separating test data from production data, and the docs say Auto-review is not a security boundary. missing for 10: explicit production-data separation or a staging/test-data environment, any guarantee that sandboxed runs cannot reach production systems, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: run in isolated VMs in the cloud with full development environments
cloud agents can build, test, and interact with the changed software
A shell command 'can run in the sandbox' when it works under the sandbox's file and network limits
Agents can start dev servers, open the app in a browser, click through UI flows, and verify their changes work before pushing a PR.
Each task gets its own files, dependencies, and changes while your main checkout stays untouched.
